title: Bengal in Depth: Kolkata, Mayapur, the Sundarbans, Mandarmani & Shantiniketan
meta_description: 11-day West Bengal itinerary: Kolkata heritage and food, ISKCON Mayapur, a Sundarbans mangrove cruise, Mandarmani beach and Tagore's Shantiniketan.
tagline: The City of Joy, the tiger's mangroves and Tagore's open-air university
facts: Comfortable, with two long day trips
intro: Bengal rewards slow travel. This route gives you Kolkata's colonial avenues, temples and food, a day at the ISKCON headquarters in Mayapur, two nights deep in the Sundarbans mangroves on a boat, a beach break at Mandarmani and the peace of Rabindranath Tagore's Shantiniketan. We changed the order of the original plan so you sleep in Kolkata between excursions instead of crossing the city twice in a day.
highlights: Victoria Memorial, Mother House, Kalighat and the Marble Palace
A full day in Mayapur, birthplace of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and ISKCON's world headquarters
Two days cruising the Sundarbans tiger reserve with watchtowers and lunch on board
Red-crab beach at Mandarmani on the Bay of Bengal
Tagore's Shantiniketan and, on Saturdays, the Sonajhuri Haat craft market
Belur Math and Dakshineswar on the last morning

days.title: Arrive in Kolkata, first look at the City of Joy
days.summary: Arrival, check-in and a half-day city tour.

rows.label: On arrival
rows.title: Meet your driver
rows.text: At the airport or Howrah station.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Half-day city tour
rows.text: Drive past the GPO, Writers' Building, Eden Gardens and Raj Bhavan; visit Mother House, St Paul's Cathedral and Victoria Memorial.
notes: Victoria Memorial museum is closed on Mondays.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Kalighat Kali Temple
rows.text: One of the 51 Shakti peethas. Go with your guide; touts at the gate are persistent.

days.note: Try mishti doi and sandesh at a sweet shop tonight. Ask us for pure-vegetarian sweet shops if you eat Jain.

days.title: Old Kolkata: Jain temple, Tagore's house and Marble Palace
days.summary: Full-day city tour with an optional evening river cruise.
strip: Marble Palace closed Monday and Thursday

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Pareshnath (Calcutta Jain) Temple
rows.text: A mirror-and-mosaic Jain temple from 1867.

rows.label: Late morning
rows.title: Jorasanko Thakur Bari
rows.text: Rabindranath Tagore's family home, now a museum.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Marble Palace
rows.text: A 19th-century mansion full of European art.
notes: Entry needs a free pass from the tourist office; we arrange it.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Optional Hooghly river cruise
rows.text: With snacks or dinner, past Howrah Bridge lit up.

days.note: Science City and Eco Park suit families with children; tell us and we swap them in.

days.title: Mayapur, home of the Hare Krishna movement
days.summary: Day trip to ISKCON Mayapur and back to Kolkata.
strip: About 130 km each way, 3.5 to 4 hours

rows.label: About 06:00
rows.title: Leave Kolkata
rows.text: Breakfast on the way.

rows.label: About 10:00
rows.title: ISKCON Mayapur
rows.text: Srila Prabhupada's Samadhi, the Radha-Madhava and Panchatattva altars, the Chaitanya exhibition and the goshala.
notes: The temple closes for darshan from about 13:00 to 16:00. We time your visit around the aartis.

rows.label: Lunch
rows.title: Govinda's prasadam restaurant
rows.text: Pure-vegetarian prasadam inside the campus.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu's birthplace and a boat at the river confluence
rows.text: Where the Jalangi meets the Ganga.

days.note: This is a long day. If you prefer, we book a guest house in Mayapur and add a night.

days.title: Into the Sundarbans mangroves
days.summary: Drive to Godkhali and cruise to Sajnekhali, with a sunset cruise past the bird sanctuary.

rows.label: About 06:30
rows.title: Drive to Godkhali jetty
rows.text: Through the villages of South 24 Parganas.

rows.label: Late morning
rows.title: Boat to Sajnekhali
rows.text: Lunch is served on the boat.

rows.label: Late afternoon
rows.title: Sunset cruise
rows.text: Past the bird sanctuary near Jatirampur.
notes: Resorts run on generators; air-conditioning usually works only from about 21:00 to 06:00.

days.note: Pack light for the Sundarbans; leave big bags at the Kolkata hotel.

days.title: Watchtowers and creeks of the tiger reserve
days.summary: Full-day boat safari: Sajnekhali, Dobanki canopy walk, Sudhanyakhali and the creeks.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Sajnekhali and Dobanki watchtowers
rows.text: Dobanki has a canopy walk caged in mesh above the forest floor.

rows.label: Midday
rows.title: Narrow creeks and the deer rehabilitation centre
rows.text: Look for crocodiles, monitor lizards, kingfishers and spotted deer.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Back towards the resort
rows.text: Tiger sightings are rare and never guaranteed; tracks on the mud banks are common.
notes: Never put hands in the water or step off the boat except at watchtowers.

days.note: Carry binoculars, a cap and mosquito repellent.

days.title: Back to Kolkata, then the beach at Mandarmani
days.summary: Morning cruise, boat to Godkhali and drive to Mandarmani.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Last creek cruise and boat to Godkhali

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Drive to Mandarmani
rows.text: We go straight to the coast so you skip a night back in the city.
notes: In the original plan this was two separate trips from Kolkata. Going straight to Mandarmani saves about 5 hours of driving.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Mandarmani beach
rows.text: A long, flat beach with red crabs at low tide.

days.note: Swim only near lifeguards; currents in the Bay of Bengal can be strong.

days.title: Beach morning and back to Kolkata
days.summary: Free morning at Mandarmani, drive to Kolkata.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Sunrise and red crabs
rows.text: Walk the beach at low tide.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Drive to Kolkata
rows.text: Evening free for New Market or Park Street.

days.note: Tonight is a good night for a Bengali vegetarian thali: shukto, cholar dal, luchi and payesh.

days.title: Tagore's Shantiniketan
days.summary: Drive to Shantiniketan and visit Visva-Bharati.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Drive north
rows.text: Breakfast at Shaktigarh, known for langcha sweets.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Visva-Bharati and Rabindra Bhavana museum
rows.text: The university Tagore founded, with classes under the trees.
notes: The campus is closed to visitors on Wednesdays, and partly on Thursdays.

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Khoai and the Sonajhuri forest
rows.text: Baul singers often perform here at sunset.

days.note: The Sonajhuri Haat craft market is busiest on Saturday afternoons. Ask us to plan your dates around it.

days.title: Back to Kolkata

rows.label: Evening
rows.title: Park Street or a heritage walk

days.note: Tomorrow's sightseeing starts at 09:00; keep packing light.

days.title: Belur Math, Dakshineswar and Howrah Bridge
days.summary: Belur Math, Dakshineswar Kali Temple and a drive over Howrah Bridge.

rows.label: Morning
rows.title: Belur Math
rows.text: Headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission, on the Ganga.
notes: Open about 06:00 to 11:30 and 16:00 to 21:00 (winter 15:30). Photography inside is not allowed.

rows.label: Midday
rows.title: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
rows.text: Where Sri Ramakrishna lived. Cross by ferry to Belur if the river is calm.

rows.label: Afternoon
rows.title: Howrah Bridge and the flower market
rows.text: Mullick Ghat flower market is busiest in the morning.

days.note: This is your last full day: tell us if you want a dinner booking.

hotel.name: Hand-picked hotels at each stop
hotel.meals: Breakfast daily; full board in the Sundarbans
hotel.about: In the Sundarbans, resorts are simple eco-lodges on generator power, not city hotels. We pick the most comfortable available.

included: Sundarbans boat, permits, guide and meals
best_time: October to March: cool, dry days for city walks and the best light in the Sundarbans. Durga Puja (September or October) is spectacular but crowded. Avoid April to June (very hot) and the monsoon from June to September.
seasons: Kolkata's biggest festival. Book hotels months ahead.
Hot and humid, then heavy monsoon rain.

faqs.q: Will we see a tiger in the Sundarbans?
faqs.a: Possibly, but sightings are rare because the tigers live in dense mangrove. You will almost certainly see crocodiles, deer, monitor lizards and many birds.

faqs.q: Is the Sundarbans comfortable for seniors?
faqs.a: Yes, with simple facilities. Boarding the boat involves a few steps on jetties, and AC works only at night.

faqs.q: Is Mayapur a good day trip?
faqs.a: It is a long day, about 4 hours each way. Devotees often prefer to add a night in the ISKCON guest houses, which we can book.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be changed for our dates and pace?
faqs.a: Yes. Every Blue Diamond Voyage itinerary is a starting point. We change the number of nights, the hotels, the pace and the activities to suit your family, and send you a personalised quote.

faqs.q: Do you look after vegetarian and Jain food?
faqs.a: Yes. We send your dietary brief to every hotel and guide before you travel, and suggest pure-vegetarian restaurants along the route. Jain meals without onion, garlic and root vegetables can be arranged in most places with notice.

entry: Aadhaar, passport, driving licence or voter ID for flights, trains and hotel check-in
Tourist e-Visa applied online before travel
Most ASI monuments sell tickets online and by UPI at the gate
About INR 20 to 50 for Indians, more for foreigners
entry_notes: Carry the original photo ID, not a photocopy. Security at airports and many temples checks it.
Phone and internet: Jio and Airtel work best across most of this route. Download offline Google Maps before hill or forest stretches, where signal drops.

good_to_know.title: UPI, cards and cash
good_to_know.text: UPI works almost everywhere, even at small stalls. Keep some cash in INR 100 and 200 notes for temples, parking, tips and places where the network is weak.

good_to_know.title: Temple and shrine etiquette
good_to_know.text: Cover shoulders and knees. Remove shoes where asked, and carry socks for hot stone floors. Leather belts and bags are not allowed inside some Jain and Hindu temples. Ask before photographing people and inside shrines.

good_to_know.title: Water and street food
good_to_know.text: Drink sealed bottled or filtered water only. Choose busy stalls where food is cooked in front of you, and skip cut fruit and ice from roadside stalls.

good_to_know.title: Driving times
good_to_know.text: Indian roads are slower than the kilometres suggest: plan on 40 to 50 km an hour on highways and much less in hills and towns. Your driver's breaks and meal stops are built into the timings.

good_to_know.title: Plugs and tipping
good_to_know.text: Plugs are Indian three-pin and two-pin, 230 volts. Tipping drivers and guides about INR 300 to 500 a day is appreciated.

dining_intro: India is the easiest country in the world for vegetarian and Jain travellers. We send your dietary brief to every hotel, and your driver knows clean, pure-vegetarian restaurants on each road day.
dining_avoid: Ask for food cooked fresh and tell the kitchen clearly if you eat Jain: no onion, garlic, ginger, potato or other root vegetables. Many dishes start with an onion-garlic base even when the menu says vegetarian.
food_card: Hum shuddh shakahari (Jain) hain. Pyaz, lahsun, adrak, aloo, gajar ya koi bhi zameen ke neeche ki sabzi nahi. Ande nahi. Kripya taaza banaiye. Dhanyavaad.
